name: Mexico (Spanish)
description: The Spanish you need for a week or two in Mexico — order food, get around, handle money, ask for help — plus enough grammar to build your own sentences, not just recite phrases.
grammarSpine: Regular present tense, I & you first: -ar/-er/-ir verbs take -o (I) and -as/-es (you). hablo/hablas, como/comes.
Tú vs usted: use usted (polite) with strangers; it takes the 'he/she' verb form (habla, ¿cómo está?).
Gender & articles: el/la, un/una; adjectives agree (-o/-a) and usually follow the noun (agua fría).
Word order is like English (subject-verb-object); to negate, put 'no' before the verb (no entiendo).
Future = voy a + verb (voy a comer = I'm going to eat). No new tense to memorize.
Power-words (fixed): quiero (I want), necesito (I need), tengo (I have), hay (there is), me gusta (I like).
ser vs estar (both 'to be'): ser for who/what something is; estar for where it is and how you feel.
